title: Reachable Within K Moves (DFS + Depth-Limited Search)
real_world_story: A robot has limited battery and can make at most K moves. The operator must know whether the charging station can be reached before the battery runs out, without searching the whole warehouse.

real_world_connection.input_represents: Warehouse grid with shelves as walls
real_world_connection.query_represents: Start position, charging station, and the move limit K
real_world_connection.algorithm_represents: Exploring deep paths first but stopping once K moves are used

problem_statement: Given an R x C maze grid of 0 (free) and 1 (wall), a start cell (sr, sc), a destination cell (dr, dc), and a move limit K, determine whether the destination can be reached from the start in at most K moves using 4-directional moves without stepping on walls.
task: Return 1 if the destination is reachable within K moves, otherwise 0.
input_format: The first line contains two integers R and C. The next R lines each contain C integers (0 or 1). The final line contains five integers sr sc dr dc K.
output_format: Print 1 if reachable within K moves, otherwise 0.

examples.explanation: The shortest route needs 4 moves, which fits exactly within K = 4.
The shortest route needs 4 moves, so K = 3 is not enough.

expected_algorithm.name: Depth-Limited Search
expected_algorithm.reason: DFS with a depth limit explores deep routes first but cuts off every path longer than K, matching a battery or lookahead budget.

complexity.time: O(4^K) worst case, O(R * C) with visited-depth pruning

hint: Stop when K < 0 or the cell is a wall or already visited on this path.
Return true as soon as the destination is found.
real_world_takeaway: Depth-limited DFS answers bounded-reachability questions without exploring the whole map.
